claims.text: One third of COVID-19 patients in the authors' autopsy study experienced a fatal pulmonary embolism.
Optimal dosing for anticoagulant treatment in patients with severe COVID-19 remains unknown and requires further prospective investigation.
Pulmonary embolism is a common but rarely fatal finding on computed tomography in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients.

evidence.description: In contrast, one third of our patients had a fatal PE.

As such, our study and that by Baldi and coworkers add substantial value to the consensus statement's claim that the 'optimal dosing [for anticoagulant treatment] in patients with severe COVID-19 remains unknown and warrants further prospective investigation.'
It is correct that PE is a common (but rarely fatal) finding on computed tomography in critically ill patients (2)...

limitations.text: Prior consensus guidance on empirical anticoagulant therapy was based mainly on a single retrospective study presenting only laboratory abnormalities without autopsy data.
VTE risk factor algorithms derived from general patients without underlying medical conditions cannot be extrapolated to patients with COVID-19.

future_work.text: Further prospective studies to determine optimal dosing for anticoagulant treatment in patients with severe COVID-19.
